record.paper_title: Variational principles in grid generation and geometric modelling: theoretical justifications and open problems
record.original_question: In a two-dimensional harmonic-coordinate grid-generation setting, a map x(u) is first obtained by minimizing the Dirichlet energy (1/2) integral tr((grad x)^T grad x) du under first-kind boundary conditions, and the useful computational grid is the inverse map u(x). After exchanging dependent and independent variables, the inverse map is governed by the nonlinear functional (1/2) integral over x(Omega) of tr((grad u)^T grad u)/det(grad u) dx. Does an existence theorem hold for this inverse-map functional, and under what precise conditions is an extremal of this functional actually the inverse of the harmonic map x(u)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded domain (the parametric/logical domain) with coordinates $u = (u^1, u^2)$, and let $D \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ be a bounded target domain with coordinates $x = (x^1, x^2)$. Consider the Dirichlet energy
$$E[x] = \frac{1}{2} \int_\Omega \operatorname{tr}\!\big((\nabla_u x)^T \nabla_u x\big)\, du$$
for maps $x : \Omega \to D$ subject to a prescribed homeomorphism boundary condition $x|_{\partial \Omega} : \partial \Omega \to \partial D$. A minimizer $x(u)$ of $E$ is a harmonic map; assume it is a diffeomorphism onto $D$, so that the inverse map $u(x) : D \to \Omega$ is well defined. After interchanging dependent and independent variables, the energy of the inverse map can be written as
$$F[u] = \frac{1}{2} \int_{D} \frac{\operatorname{tr}\!\big((\nabla_x u)^T \nabla_x u\big)}{\det (\nabla_x u)}\, dx,$$
to be considered over orientation-preserving maps $u : D \to \Omega$ with $\det(\nabla_x u) > 0$ a.e.\ and matching boundary correspondence $u|_{\partial D} = (x|_{\partial \Omega})^{-1}$.

Questions:
1. Establish an existence theorem for minimizers (or, more generally, extremals) of the functional $F$ within a suitable class of orientation-preserving Sobolev mappings with the prescribed boundary correspondence.
2. Identify precise conditions (on the domains, the boundary correspondence, and the admissible class) under which every extremal of $F$ is exactly the inverse of the harmonic map $x(u)$ minimizing $E$.
artifact.status_search_result: Search results discuss variational forms of the Winslow (inverse-harmonic) grid generator and note that solving the inverse harmonic formulation yields non-folding grids with nonvanishing Jacobian, but no source provides a complete existence theorem for the inverse-map functional together with a characterization of when its extremals coincide with the inverse of the harmonic map. The status of the precise question therefore appears unresolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: A Variational Form of the Winslow Grid Generator
status_evidence.snippet: Variational formulation of the Winslow (inverse harmonic) grid generator.
status_evidence.claim: A variational form of the inverse-harmonic functional has been studied but a complete existence/equivalence theorem is not stated.

status_evidence.title: Theory of harmonic grid generation-II
status_evidence.snippet: Solving the harmonic equations in the inverse formulation guarantees a nonvanishing Jacobian.
status_evidence.claim: The inverse harmonic formulation is known to give unfolded grids, but a rigorous existence theorem for the inverse functional is not provided.

status_evidence.title: A Framework for Variational Grid Generation
status_evidence.snippet: Variational grid-generation framework based on Jacobian matrix norms.
status_evidence.claim: Related variational frameworks exist but do not settle the precise existence and equivalence question for the inverse harmonic functional.
